prerequisites: Physics in 2nd year of high school (recommended)
Mathematical knowledge of vector calculus, trigonometry, and differentiation and integration of single-variable functions (recommended)

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the physicomathematical description of particle motion and know the magnitudes that quantify it.
Understand the laws and theorems that relate the motion of particles with the causes that provoke it.
Understand the concepts and principles necessary for the study of heat exchange processes in closed systems of ideal gases.
Correctly handle the recommended physical symbology, both in terms of magnitudes and units.
Learn and apply problem-solving strategies related to the different contents of the course.
Acquire the skills related to laboratory work and the treatment of measurements and errors.
Knowledge of basic subjects and technologies, that enable students to learn new methods and technologies, as well as provide great versatility to adapt to new situations.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities, understanding the ethical and professional responsibility of the Telecommunications Technical Engineer's activity.
Knowledge for performing measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, task planning and other similar works in their specific field of telecommunications.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts about the general laws of mechanics and thermodynamics and their application to solve problems typical of engineering.

syllabus_topics: Physical magnitudes. Treatment of measurement errors.
Dynamics of the particle: Work and energy.
Thermometry and calorimetry. First law of thermodynamics.
teaching_methods: Expositive classes (lectures and explanations of theoretical content, examples, problem-solving, group evaluation activities)
Classroom practices/Seminars/Workshops (problem-solving, group work activities, presentation and defense of problems/works/projects, small group evaluation activities)
Laboratory practices (handling measurement equipment, use of simulation/data processing software, analysis of results and report writing, very small group evaluation activities)
Problem-solving and preparation of practice reports, works
assessment_rules: The final grade (NFO) is calculated as EvC + (1 – EvC/10) × CGO, where EvC is the continuous assessment grade (CPA + CCS + CPL) and CGO is the global exam grade. This formula is applied only if a minimum of 3.5 points (out of 10) is achieved in the global exam (CGO) and a minimum global score of 2.0 points (out of 5.5) is achieved in continuous assessment (EvC). If the minimums are not met or if continuous assessment is lost, the final grade (NFE) will be equal to the global exam grade (CGE or CGO). A final grade below 5.0 points results in a FAIL.
